l4_steps.name: Receive engine from aircraft and log induction
l4_steps.input: Engine removal notification from line maintenance or heavy check
l4_steps.output: Engine induction record with serial number, TSN, CSN, and removal reason
l4_steps.kpi: Induction record created within 4 hours of engine receipt
l4_steps.pain_point: Incomplete removal documentation from line stations delays accurate TSN/CSN capture, risking life-limit tracking errors in AMOS

l4_steps.name: Perform incoming borescope inspection of engine
l4_steps.input: Induction record, engine removal reason, last borescope findings
l4_steps.output: Borescope inspection report with blade condition, FOD, and erosion findings
l4_steps.kpi: Borescope inspection completed within 24 hours of induction; findings logged in AMOS within 2 hours of inspection
l4_steps.pain_point: FOD damage discovered at induction not captured in aircraft logbook leads to retroactive safety investigations under FAR Part 43.9 and delays work scope confirmation

l4_steps.name: Determine shop visit type and open work order
l4_steps.input: Borescope report, engine removal reason, performance trend data
l4_steps.output: Shop visit classification (Performance Restoration, HSI, or On-Condition) and AMOS work order
l4_steps.kpi: Work order opened and shop visit type confirmed within 8 hours of induction
l4_steps.pain_point: Performance trend data from on-wing ACARS monitoring (SITA ACARS) may not sync to AMOS automatically, forcing manual EGT margin entry and introducing transcription errors

l4_steps.name: Disassemble engine modules per CMM procedures
l4_steps.input: AMOS work order, OEM Component Maintenance Manual (CMM), tooling list
l4_steps.output: Disassembled engine modules staged for inspection; AMOS task cards signed off
l4_steps.kpi: Module teardown completed within published CMM man-hour estimate ±10%
l4_steps.pain_point: OEM CMM revision cycle (Boeing/CFM/GE) lags regulatory changes; AMOS document revision alerts can be suppressed by users, risking use of superseded procedures

l4_steps.name: Inspect HPC, HPT, LPT, and fan modules
l4_steps.input: Disassembled modules, OEM Airworthiness Limitations (AWL), AD compliance matrix
l4_steps.output: Module inspection findings report; life-limited part (LLP) status updated in AMOS
l4_steps.kpi: 100% LLP cycle verification against AMOS life-limit records; inspection findings report issued within 48 hours of module receipt
l4_steps.pain_point: LLP cycle counter discrepancies between AMOS and Boeing Toolbox / CAMP cause certification holds; reconciliation requires manual cross-check, averaging 6–8 hours per engine

l4_steps.name: Identify AD/SB compliance gaps and raise EOs
l4_steps.input: Module inspection report, FAA AD database, OEM service bulletin index
l4_steps.output: Engineering Orders (EOs) raised in AMOS for each open AD/SB; updated work scope
l4_steps.kpi: Zero open mandatory ADs at engine release; all applicable SBs evaluated within 24 hours of findings report
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA AD compliance is checked against AMOS AD library which requires manual updates; a delayed AD import (>30 days) creates regulatory exposure under FAR Part 91.409 and Part 43 Appendix D

l4_steps.name: Classify parts as BER, serviceable, or repairable
l4_steps.input: Teardown findings report, OEM serviceability limits, repair cost benchmarks
l4_steps.output: Parts disposition list with BER (Beyond Economic Repair), serviceable, and repair-route tags in AMOS
l4_steps.kpi: Parts disposition completed within 48 hours of teardown; BER rate benchmarked at ≤15% of total parts count
l4_steps.pain_point: BER decisions without OEM-approved repair data require Designated Engineering Representative (DER) approval under FAR Part 145.109, adding 3–10 days per non-standard repair route

l4_steps.name: Check rotable parts availability in pool
l4_steps.input: Parts disposition list, rotable pool inventory records
l4_steps.output: Availability confirmation or shortage list for critical engine parts
l4_steps.kpi: Rotable pool fill rate ≥85% for engine shop demand; critical part shortage identified within 4 hours of disposition
l4_steps.pain_point: CAMP and AMOS rotable inventory records are not always real-time synced; double-allocation of serviceable parts across concurrent shop visits causes last-minute shortages and AOG escalations

l4_steps.name: Raise purchase orders for parts shortages
l4_steps.input: Shortage list from CAMP, approved vendor list (AVL), engine TAT deadline
l4_steps.output: SAP Ariba purchase orders for parts; expected delivery dates entered in AMOS parts tracking
l4_steps.kpi: PO raised within 8 hours of shortage confirmation; expedited orders for AOG parts placed within 2 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: SAP Ariba approved vendor list (AVL) may not include all OEM-authorised repair vendors; purchasing outside AVL requires Finance exception approval adding 24–48 hours to critical-path parts

l4_steps.name: Repair and overhaul modules per CMM
l4_steps.input: Module inspection report, EOs, CMM repair procedures, serviceable replacement parts
l4_steps.output: Repaired modules with AMOS task cards signed; NDT records attached
l4_steps.kpi: Repair man-hours within ±15% of AMOS work-order estimate; first-pass quality rate ≥92%
l4_steps.pain_point: Specialised repair capabilities (e.g., HPT blade tip restore, HPC coating) often require sub-vendor routing; each external repair adds 7–21 days TAT and requires dual-release documentation under EASA Part 145.A.75

l4_steps.name: Apply approved modifications and service bulletins
l4_steps.input: Open SB list from Step 2.3, OEM modification kits, Engineering Orders
l4_steps.output: Modification compliance records in AMOS; updated engine configuration baseline
l4_steps.kpi: 100% mandatory SB incorporation confirmed before assembly; optional SB cost/benefit review completed within 4 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: OEM modification kit availability is frequently constrained (CFM LEAP kits lead times 90–180 days); planning teams must lock SB scope 6+ months before shop visit to avoid TAT overruns

l4_steps.name: Reassemble engine and verify build standard
l4_steps.input: Repaired and serviceable modules, torque specifications, build standard document
l4_steps.output: Fully assembled engine; AMOS build record with component serial numbers and final configuration
l4_steps.kpi: Assembly completed within 48 hours of all parts arrival; dimensional check non-conformance rate ≤5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Configuration mismatch between AMOS build record and physical engine (e.g., wrong fan blade set) is not caught until test cell, costing 12–24 hours of re-teardown time

l4_steps.name: Install engine on test cell and configure parameters
l4_steps.input: Assembled engine, test cell acceptance test procedure (ATP), engine spec sheet
l4_steps.output: Engine installed on test cell; baseline parameters configured in Trax test run record
l4_steps.kpi: Test cell installation completed within 4 hours; test cell utilisation rate ≥80%
l4_steps.pain_point: Test cell scheduling conflicts between engine shop and contracted MRO customers reduce throughput; dynamic slot allocation is managed manually via spreadsheet, not integrated with AMOS shop scheduling

l4_steps.name: Run engine acceptance test per ECTM limits
l4_steps.input: OEM Acceptance Test Procedure (ATP), Engine Condition Trend Monitoring (ECTM) limits, test cell instrumentation data
l4_steps.output: Test run data report: EGT margin, fuel flow, vibration, oil consumption vs. OEM limits
l4_steps.kpi: EGT margin ≥25°C at end-of-test; vibration ≤0.5 in/sec; oil consumption ≤0.5 qt/hr
l4_steps.pain_point: ECTM limits defined in Trax must match the engine variant spec sheet; configuration mismatch between test cell software version and OEM ATP revision causes out-of-tolerance alerts that require manual waiver processing

l4_steps.name: Complete FAA 8130-3 / EASA Form 1 release docs
l4_steps.input: Test cell certification, AMOS work order completion data, AD/SB compliance records
l4_steps.output: FAA 8130-3 or EASA Form 1 Authorised Release Certificate; closed AMOS work order
l4_steps.kpi: Release documentation completed within 8 hours of test cell sign-off; zero documentation deficiencies at FAA/EASA audit
l4_steps.pain_point: Dual-release requirements (FAA 8130-3 and EASA Form 1) for engines operated on international routes require two signatories with current authorisations; signatory availability is a recurring bottleneck, especially on night shifts

l4_steps.name: Update engine life history and rotable records
l4_steps.input: Closed AMOS work order, LLP cycle updates, modification compliance records
l4_steps.output: Updated engine life history in CAMP; rotable pool inventory record updated with new TSO/CSO
l4_steps.kpi: Engine history updated within 4 hours of work order closure; LLP discrepancy rate ≤0.1% at next audit
l4_steps.pain_point: CAMP and AMOS are not bidirectionally integrated in all configurations; manual re-entry of cycle counts from AMOS into CAMP introduces transcription errors that create airworthiness record discrepancies requiring DFP investigation

l4_steps.name: Obtain QA airworthiness release approval
l4_steps.input: Complete AMOS work order, release certificate, CAMP history update confirmation
l4_steps.output: QA-signed airworthiness release; engine cleared for return to rotable pool or direct fitment
l4_steps.kpi: QA release granted within 4 hours of documentation package submission; zero engines released with open corrective actions
l4_steps.pain_point: QA holds caused by incomplete corrective action evidence in AMOS (e.g., missing NDT report attachments) are the leading cause of engine release delays, averaging 6–12 hours per incident

l4_steps.name: Return engine to rotable pool and notify planning
l4_steps.input: QA airworthiness release, engine storage requirements, fleet demand forecast
l4_steps.output: Engine tagged serviceable in AMOS rotable pool; network planning team notified of availability
l4_steps.kpi: Engine available in rotable pool within 2 hours of QA release; total shop visit TAT vs. target reported monthly
l4_steps.pain_point: Rotable pool engine availability is not directly visible in SkyWORKS fleet assignment planning; network and maintenance planning teams rely on manual notifications, creating misalignment between engine availability and scheduled aircraft return-to-service dates
